implementation.name: Cython 3 Python-extension compiler
implementation.version_scope: Cython 3 and its documented in-place extension workflow; Python and the native C toolchain are separate prerequisites.

sources.label: Cython two-stage native extension build
Cython static types, conversion and overflow behavior
Cython Apache licence

fit.text: Build Python extension modules and add C-level types where measured workload behavior justifies them.

prerequisites.text: Install Cython, Python build support and a compatible C compiler; generated extensions must be importable by the selected Python.

execution.text: Cython translates .pyx/.py to C, then a native compiler produces a .so or Windows .pyd extension.

behavior.text: C types change arithmetic semantics: conversion to an int can raise OverflowError, while C arithmetic overflow is not checked.

tooling.text: Use setuptools for packaged builds, cythonize -i for a small in-place module or notebook integration for exploration.

maintenance.text: Pure-Python typing syntax benefits from Cython 3; preserve both Cython and native build settings when distributing extensions.

costs.text: The compiler is Apache-2.0; Python, native libraries and build-tool dependencies have separate terms.

example.code:
def total(int first, int second, int third):
    return first + second + third
example.run_instructions: With Python, Cython, setuptools and a supported C compiler installed, run cythonize -i totals.pyx. In the same directory run python -c "from totals import total; print(total(2, 4, 6))".
example.expected_result: The imported extension function returns 12, which Python prints.

licenses.scope: Named implementation only; dependencies and generated applications require separate review.
licenses.notice: Retain the implementation license and relevant notices when redistributing it.

fit.text: Write native systems and application programs with modules, templates and direct OS interfaces.

prerequisites.text: Install DMD and its linker/runtime environment; imports make module declarations available without a separate header workflow.

execution.text: dmd -run compiles, links and runs a source for a quick local entry; ordinary builds produce a persistent executable.

behavior.text: Garbage collection coexists with RAII and explicit resource management; contracts express preconditions, postconditions and invariants.

tooling.text: The compiler provides unit-test, documentation, profiling and diagnostic options; the standard-library reference covers Phobos.

maintenance.text: Release switches change checks: documented -release behavior disables contracts/asserts and changes some bounds checking.

costs.text: DMD and Phobos have Boost-1.0 terms; keep distinct compiler and library notices when redistributing their source.

example.run_instructions: With DMD and its platform toolchain installed, run dmd -run sum.d.

execution.text: Verification checks obligations without requiring a generated executable; build/run additionally invoke the chosen target's toolchain.

behavior.text: Method contracts and assertions constrain modeled behavior; termination and bounds obligations also matter.

tooling.text: IDE integrations run verification during editing; target compilation needs the relevant .NET, Java or other backend tools.

prerequisites.text: Install dhall-json and learn records/functions plus basic CLI use; the tutorial documents Windows, macOS and Linux packages.

execution.text: The tools evaluate a Dhall expression and serialize its result as JSON or YAML.

behavior.text: Dhall rejects mixed-type lists; external effects are limited to importing expressions from files, environment or remote sources.

tooling.text: dhall-to-json supports file input and explanatory errors; dhall-to-yaml shares the documented expression workflow.

maintenance.text: Keep language/package versions aligned: the tutorial explicitly excludes older converters for some of its features.

costs.text: The selected Haskell implementation has BSD-3-Clause terms; imported configurations and consuming applications have independent licensing.

example.run_instructions: With dhall-to-json installed, run dhall-to-json --file app.dhall.
example.expected_result: The tool emits a JSON object equivalent to {"app":"PLLDN","retries":3,"enabled":true}; formatting and field order can differ.

fit.text: Build native applications and libraries organized into Dylan libraries and modules.

prerequisites.text: Install Open Dylan and its platform build tools; deft and dylan-compiler must be available on PATH.

execution.text: deft creates an application project and builds it; executables and compiled libraries are placed in _build.

behavior.text: Each source file declares its module; top-level expressions execute in order when the library is loaded.

tooling.text: The project includes library/module definitions, ordered .lid files, source registries and a dependency manifest.

maintenance.text: Use documentation matching the release: project generation changed from dylan to deft after Open Dylan 2024.1.

costs.text: The implementation has MIT portions, CMU/Gwydion acknowledgement conditions and a BSD-2-Clause memory pool; retain component notices.

example.run_instructions: With the current Open Dylan tools installed, run deft new application --simple hello-world and enter that directory. Replace hello-world.dylan with this code, preserving the generated library/module definitions. Run deft build --all, then _build/bin/hello-world; Windows launch details are linked from the guide.

fit.text: Develop object-oriented application systems using classes, reusable components and explicit contracts.

prerequisites.text: Install a selected EiffelStudio edition; learn class creation routines and require/ensure/invariant concepts.

execution.text: The publisher's starter compiles a class file with ec; the installed project/toolchain governs how the application is launched.

behavior.text: Preconditions, postconditions and invariants express component assumptions and can serve as runtime checks.

tooling.text: EiffelStudio supplies an IDE with code/design browsing, a debugger, metrics and profiling.

maintenance.text: Resolve licensing against the selected distribution: the repository README's GPL statement conflicts with an overriding proprietary Root-LICENSE notice.

costs.text: The vendor distinguishes non-commercial Personal licences from commercial Professional licences; platform and support choices affect the purchased product.

example.code:
class HELLO_WORLD
create
    make
feature
    make
        do
            print ("PLLDN%N")
        end
end
example.run_instructions: With an appropriately licensed EiffelStudio installed, save this class as hello_world.e and run ec hello_world.e as documented by the publisher. Launch the resulting application using that installation's build/run output.
example.expected_result: Running the application prints PLLDN followed by a newline.

licenses.notice: The README says GPL v2, while Root LICENSE.txt claims proprietary restrictions and explicitly overrides file notices. Verify the selected release's agreement; an SPDX GPL grant is not asserted here.

fit.text: Build browser interfaces with state, rendered HTML and updates driven by messages.

prerequisites.text: Install Elm and a suitable editor; elm init creates elm.json plus the source directory.

execution.text: elm make produces browser HTML or JavaScript; a JavaScript build exposes a module initialization function.

behavior.text: The application model stores state, the view renders it, and update transforms it in response to messages.

tooling.text: Use elm reactor for local examples and elm make for distributable output; elm install adds dependencies.

maintenance.text: Check JavaScript requirements against flags, ports and custom elements before embedding existing widgets or unsupported browser APIs.

costs.text: The compiler uses BSD-3-Clause; application packages and integrated JavaScript libraries retain their own licences.

example.code:
module Main exposing (main)

import Html exposing (text)

main =
    text "PLLDN"
example.run_instructions: Run elm init in a project directory and save this file as src/Main.elm. Run elm make src/Main.elm, then open the generated index.html in a browser.
